title: Mirabel and the Harbor
premise: In 1911, Ines Kavanagh, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Meridian Trading Company in a fog-bound harbor town, has survived by being useful and unseen. When the seasonal bridge closes, stranding the town, he learns that Sefa, a diver's daughter who once saved his life, is now branded an enemy of the company after her father led a strike — and she is hiding in the flooded caves beneath the harbor, waiting for a boat that will never come. Bound by a promise made before the orders came down, Ines smuggles food, medicine, and finally himself into the caves while the company's enforcer, Mr. Quill, closes in. The story ends with Ines burning his indenture papers to light the way out through the caves at spring tide, choosing open defiance over invisibility, as Sefa escapes by sea and he stays behind to face the company — no longer invisible, but no longer alone.
about_author: Petra Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers from the Pacific pearling era. She writes from a coastal cottage where the tide charts on her wall are older than the house.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Ines Kavanagh inventories his life in portable things: a knife, a mother's shell comb, his indenture papers. POV: Ines. Establishes his philosophy of survival through lightness and invisibility within the Meridian Trading Company compound. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Weighing House
chapters.summary: Ines delivers the season's pearl haul and witnesses Quill, the company enforcer, shortchange a diver named Tevake. POV: Ines. He says nothing, and hates himself for it. Emotional beat: the first crack in his belief that silence is safety.

chapters.title: Sefa of the Shallows
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: three years earlier, Sefa pulled drowning Ines from a failed dive, and he promised her anything she ever asked. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: warmth and debt entangled; the promise that will define him.

chapters.title: Orders Come Down
chapters.summary: The company declares the divers' strike committee enemies of its contract; Tevake's name tops the list. Boats are confiscated, rations cut. POV: Ines, watching from the counting room. Emotional beat: fear spreading like oil on water.

chapters.title: Last Crossing
chapters.summary: The bridge closes for the storm season with Ines on the wrong side of it, trapped in the harbor town among the strikers he was meant to watch. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the road out is gone, and so is his excuse.

chapters.title: A Knock at Low Tide
chapters.summary: A child slips Ines a note: Sefa is alive, hiding in the flooded sea caves, declared enemy alongside her father. She asks for what he promised. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror and terrible gratitude arriving together.

chapters.title: Bread Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Ines begins stealing from his own ration allotment, hiding bread in the false bottom of his dive basket. POV: Ines, with mounting paranoia. Emotional beat: the physical cost of a promise — hunger, sleeplessness, doubled shadows.

chapters.title: Quill Takes Notice
chapters.summary: Quill interviews Ines about the missing rations, courteous and surgical. Ines lies well enough to survive the hour but not the week. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience versus the liar's exhaustion.

chapters.title: Into the Caves
chapters.summary: At ebb tide, Ines swims the submerged passage and finds Sefa — thinner, unbroken, furious that he waited so long. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: reunion as confrontation; love expressed as accusation.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Sefa shows him the cave community: divers' families surviving on rainwater and mussels. Ines realizes his 'enemy' is a whole village. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: A Boat That Will Never Come
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the plan: a sympathetic skipper was to take them out before the bridge closed. The boat is gone. Spring tide, six weeks off, is their only window. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: hope downsized to arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Someone in the caves is selling information; a search party comes within a lantern's reach of the entrance. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: betrayal inside sanctuary — trust becomes a rationed good.

chapters.title: Mother's Comb
chapters.summary: Ines trades his last keepsake to a smuggler for quinine when fever sweeps the caves. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief for the boy who measured life in portable things.

chapters.title: Quill's Offer
chapters.summary: Quill corners Ines: inform on the caves and earn his freedom papers, or hang beside them when the bridge reopens. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Long Watch
chapters.summary: Ines spends a sleepless night between two worlds — the compound that owns him, the caves that need him — and drafts two letters he'll never send. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the still point before the fall.

chapters.title: Tevake's Grave
chapters.summary: Tevake dies of the fever; the caves bury him at low tide. Sefa asks Ines not what he promised, but who he intends to be. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mourning crystallized into decision.

chapters.title: Burned Edge
chapters.summary: Ines discovers the informer is a starving boy blackmailed by Quill — and covers for him, turning the leak into a channel of false information. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: False Tide
chapters.summary: Using the boy, Ines feeds Quill a fake escape date; the enforcer commits his men to the wrong cove. POV: Ines, breathless with the audacity of it. Emotional beat: the hunted becoming the architects.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: The real escape night: storm-swollen seas, one borrowed skiff, and Quill returning early, suspicious. Ines must hold the cave mouth alone. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into clarity.

chapters.title: The Papers
chapters.summary: Cornered by Quill, Ines burns his indenture papers in a signal lamp to guide Sefa's skiff through the reef gap — destroying his own legal existence to save hers. Climax. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: liberation and ruin in a single flame.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Keeps
chapters.summary: Sefa reaches open water; Ines is taken, beaten, and held for the magistrate coming with the reopened bridge. But the divers refuse to dive, and the company cannot survive without pearls. POV: Ines, from a cell. Emotional beat: cost acknowledged, spirit intact.

chapters.title: Carried
chapters.summary: Facing the magistrate, Ines finds the whole diving community standing witness — the invisible made visible. His indenture voided, he walks out past Quill onto the reopened bridge, carrying nothing, owed everything. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: resolution — identity chosen, price paid, promise kept.
